Bring your team to Dental Implant Conference

The 2026 Dental Implant Conference in Chicago, Ill., offers an opportunity to strengthen your relationships with referring colleagues and other members of your restorative team. Whether you make it a group trip to the Windy City or learn from the comfort of your office, you can share a promotional code that gives your colleagues a discount on registration. Visit AAOMS.org/DICspecial to learn more.

This year’s Conference will have something for everyone and will challenge assumptions through the theme Implant Truth Wars: What We Think We Know vs. What the Data Actually Show. Topics to be covered include esthetic zone implants, peri-implant disease, immediate placement and immediate load, full-arch risk management, digital planning and artificial intelligence, bone regeneration and more.

To register, visit AAOMS.org/DIC.

Latest JOMS online

The October edition of the Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery is available to read online. Featured articles include:

  • Training Matters: Why Competency Should Guide Office-Based Pediatric Anesthesia Policy
  • Predictors of New-Onset Anxiety or Depression Following Open Reduction and Internal Fixation of Mandible Fractures
  • Preauricular Approach for Removal of a Displaced Dental Implant From the Infratemporal Fossa: A Case Report
  • Is Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon Experience Associated With Antibiotic Prescribing to Medicare Beneficiaries?

Visit AAOMS.org/JOMS to read.

Don’t miss discount on online assistants course

Did you know that AAOMS offers a completely online alternative to the Anesthesia Assistants Review Course? And for this month only, you can sign up staff at a discounted rate. The On-Line Anesthesia Review for Dental Anesthesia Assistants focuses on the principles of anesthesia administration and patient monitoring and helps assistants prepare for the Dental Anesthesia Assistant National Certification Examination (DAANCE). Participants can study at their own pace for up to 45 days and learn at home, in the office or anywhere.

Register by Oct. 31 to save $75 on registration. Visit AAOMS.org/OMSstaff to register today.

Register for upcoming webinars

As oral and maxillofacial surgeons, we may not always consider the effect patient nutrition can have on surgical outcomes. On Nov. 18, AAOMS will present the webinar The Role of Nutrition in Healing after Maxillofacial Surgery, which will explore the evidence connecting diet with alveolar bone metabolism and wound healing. The 60-minute webinar also will cover practical strategies for evaluating and optimizing serum micronutrient levels before surgery to support healing.

A 90-minute webinar on Nov. 11 will break down the complexities of reporting E/M services in OMS practice, covering office and outpatient visits, emergency room encounters, inpatient follow-ups and distinctions between consultations and evaluations/exams. Using real world scenarios and practical examples, the E/M Coding Simplified: Guidelines for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery webinar also will clarify medical decision-making, time based reporting and the correct use of modifiers 24, 25 and 57 to support accurate coding and proper reimbursement.

And don’t miss out on the Resident Wellness Webinar: Navigating Mental Health as an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon next Tuesday. Open to all members of the Association – not just residents – this complimentary webinar will offer a discussion of factors contributing to mental health challenges among surgeons as well as strategies for managing these challenges, building resilience and protecting well-being.

Register at AAOMS.org/Webinars.

District V wins OMSPAC House of Delegates Challenge

At the 2026 AAOMS Annual Meeting, OMSPAC hosted its fifth annual House of Delegates Challenge, which was won by District V with the highest per capita contribution. Districts I, II, IV and V reached 100 percent participation. Delegates and Alternates had an overall participation rate of over 92 percent. Thank you for your support!

Celebrating a community of giving

The 2026 AAOMS Annual Meeting in Seattle brought members together to support the OMS Foundation in a variety of ways. From purchasing Foundation socks, participating in the morning Health Walks and attending the OMS Foundation Alliance Luncheon and Donor Appreciation Reception, more than $30,000 was raised during the week. Dr. Jeffrey Wallen’s $25,000 gift match brought the total to more than $55,000. Thank you to everyone who donated, visited the Foundation booth or participated in Foundation activities.
